speaker: Marcus Webb
cascadeSummary: The C113-approved Month-12 $400,000 disbursement is executed this cycle — the twelfth consecutive monthly check to reach the long-tenure West Oakland cohort, the 23-day processing standard held. I published the Month-12 closeout and expenditure reconciliation alongside it, because Councilmember Crane asked and because my files were already ready. Charter renewal drafting moves to scope-preservation language: the long-tenure West Oakland cohort stays the cohort. Grand Lake's $2.5M advances to a recorded full-council decision with the Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions intact — I don't presume passage and I don't drop the conditions.

statements.topic: Month-12 disbursement executed and closeout published
statements.decision: Execute the C113-approved Month-12 $400,000 disbursement under the 23-day processing standard and publish the Month-12 closeout and expenditure reconciliation in the same release.
statements.quote: Twelve months, twelve checks — and this time the closeout lands on the same day as the disbursement, not a cycle after it.
statements.fullStatement: The Month-12 $400,000 disbursement is executed as of this cycle. That is the twelfth consecutive monthly tranche to reach the long-tenure West Oakland cohort, and the 23-day average processing standard held through it. What I want the public and the Council to see is that the closeout and the expenditure reconciliation went out with the check, not behind it. Councilmember Crane asked for published Month-12 closeout records before charter renewal drafting advances, and that is a fair ask — my files were already assembled by the time the question arrived. The reconciliation shows every dollar of this tranche against its case file: intake date, eligibility finding, authorization, and paid receipt. If a reporter walks the third floor of the OEWD building this week, they will see the green folder spines updated on the status board and the paid receipts filed in the same drawer as the determinations. That is what month twelve looks like on the ground — not a ribbon, a reconciliation.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Month-12 $400K disbursement executed; closeout and expenditure reconciliation published same release; 23-day standard held.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Charter renewal draft completion preserving West Oakland cohort scope; Month-12 closeout review at Council

statements.decision: Advance charter renewal drafting with the Fund's scope explicitly preserved to West Oakland businesses and residents as chartered, and publish the draft language for review alongside the closeout record.
statements.quote: The charter named a cohort and a neighborhood. The renewal draft names them back — no quiet rewrite.
statements.fullStatement: Charter renewal drafting moves to the drafting desk this cycle, and the scope language is the part I will not let drift. The Fund serves West Oakland businesses and residents — that is the C109 scope correction and it is what the renewal has to say on its face. I have heard the concern that a renewal is where scope gets quietly widened or narrowed in a subclause, and I take it seriously enough that the draft will be published in full rather than summarized. What I can tell you concretely about the drafting process: the renewal carries forward the 23-day processing standard as an operating commitment, carries forward the district-equity tracking we built into the month-eight through month-twelve tranches, and carries forward the audit criteria that have kept every case file defensible. What it does not carry is an expansion of the program's reach into neighborhoods the charter did not name. Downtown is a separate initiative and I will not let a renewal clause blur that line. When the draft is complete it goes to the Council record with the closeout documentation attached, so the two can be read together.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Charter renewal drafting advanced with scope-preservation language (West Oakland businesses and residents); draft to publish with closeout record.

statements.topic: Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake — recorded council decision with conditions intact
statements.decision: Support a recorded full-council decision on the $2.5M Grand Lake proposal with the Chen-Vega milestone and audit conditions intact, and require public milestone reporting — without presuming the vote's outcome.
statements.quote: Grand Lake's $2.5 million goes to a vote with every milestone and audit condition still attached — and I don't get to write the result in advance.
statements.fullStatement: Commercial Stabilization for Grand Lake advanced to full council last cycle with the Chen-Vega milestone and audit conditions in place, and my position this cycle is that those conditions stay exactly where they are. The Mayor's agenda calls for a recorded full-council decision with the conditions intact and public reporting required, and that is the right frame — a recorded decision means residents can find the vote and read what was attached to it. The engine flagged a low-severity improvement item on this initiative and I want to be precise about what that means in my shop: it is an implementation note, not a finding. It does not change the conditions, it does not clear the vote, and it does not presume passage. What I can tell you operationally is that the milestone-reporting template is already drafted and the audit criteria are carried over from the stabilization framework I administer — the same case-file discipline, applied to a commercial program. If the council records a yes, the first milestone report is due on the schedule in the conditions. If it records a no, the template goes in the drawer and stays there. Either way the record is public.

trackerUpdates.MilestoneNotes: C114: Grand Lake $2.5M carried to recorded full-council decision with Chen-Vega milestones and audit conditions intact; milestone-reporting template drafted.
trackerUpdates.NextScheduledAction: Recorded full-council decision with conditions intact; first milestone report upon authorization

statements.decision: Keep the Saturday Adeline Street intake desk staffed, hold the 23-day processing standard through renewal, and keep the West Oakland cohort at the front of the queue as the $400,000 Month-12 tranche clears.
statements.quote: The people of West Oakland do not need a narrator. They need the queue to move and the case file to hold — and I will answer for both.
statements.fullStatement: The mood in West Oakland this cycle is good — street trade is busy, the block is quiet, and I am not going to pretend that mood is mine to claim. What I will claim is the part I answer for: the queue. The Saturday intake desk on Adeline Street stays staffed through the renewal process, because the moment the program looks like it is winding down is the moment the rumor outruns the reality and people stop coming in with files that are eligible. The 23-day standard holds. The case files stay where they are — in the cabinets, color-coded on the board, updated before I leave at night — because the households in this cohort have waited long enough in this program's history that a slow cycle is not an abstraction to them. What West Oakland gets from this desk this cycle is a twelfth check, a published reconciliation, and a renewal draft that names them back. And when Carla Edmonds calls about a specific applicant, she gets a call back with the case status and the reason for it, not a statement.
